issues.failure_explanation:
The prose claims the listed integrability conditions on the coefficient derivatives of the quasilinear model suffice, via Holder's inequality and the Sobolev embedding, to control all terms of eq:DF-ql for any fixed admissible p. For the term \int \partial_s A \,\delta u\,
abla v with \partial_s A \in L^{p/2}, \delta u \in L^{p}, 
abla v \in L^{2}, Holder requires 2/p + 1/p + 1/2 <= 1, i.e. p >= 6. The same restriction arises for \int \partial_p B \,
abla\delta u\, v with \partial_p B \in L^{p/2}. For p < 6 (admissible in both d = 2 and d = 3) the Holder exponents sum to more than 1 and the product is not guaranteed to be integrable, so the stated conditions are not sufficient. They work only for p >= 6 (in 3D only at p = 6).

failure_location.quote:
so that all terms in \eqref{eq:DF-ql} are controlled by H\"older's inequality together with the Sobolev
embedding for a fixed admissible $p$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the sufficiency claim to p >= 6 (in 2D, p in [6, infinity); in 3D, p = 6), or strengthen the coefficient integrability conditions (e.g. require \partial_s A and \partial_p B in L^r with r >= 2p/(p+2)) to cover p < 6.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficiency claim for well-definedness of the quasilinear linearisation eq:DF-ql is unsupported over most of the stated admissible range of p. Formal results that assume Frechet differentiability abstractly are not directly invalidated, but a reader relying on the listed conditions for p < 6 may apply the framework to a model whose derivative is not well-defined.
issues.title: Sufficient integrability conditions for quasilinear derivative fail for p < 6
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local condition change (add the restriction p >= 6 or adjust the exponents) that preserves every formal result, the method, and the guarantee. No new lemma, construction, or proof architecture is needed; the semilinear conditions remain correct for all p and the numerical experiments are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation:
The adjoint residual \langle\mathcal G(z_h),vangle = \int s_h^{\ast} v - \int A
abla z_h\cdot
abla v has effective (physical) flux A^{\ast} = -A
abla z_h, the coefficient of 
abla v. Applying the residual-split template of eq:res_split, which pairs the equilibrated flux with the physical flux as (\mathfrak A - \sigma_h), gives the flux-mismatch norm \|\sigma_h^{\ast} - A^{\ast}\|_{A_0^{-1}} = \|\sigma_h^{\ast} + A
abla z_h\|_{A_0^{-1}}, not \|\sigma_h^{\ast} - A
abla z_h\|_{A_0^{-1}} as written. When \|\sigma_h^{\ast} - A
abla z_h\| < \|\sigma_h^{\ast} + A
abla z_h\| the resulting bound on \|\mathcal G(z_h)\|_{V^{\ast}} is too small and the adjoint-enhanced enclosure is not guaranteed to contain the true output.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Replace the flux-mismatch term \|\sigma_h^{\ast}-A
abla z_h\|_{A_0^{-1}} with \|\sigma_h^{\ast}+A
abla z_h\|_{A_0^{-1}} (equivalently \|\sigma_h^{\ast}-(-A
abla z_h)\|_{A_0^{-1}}). The element residual R_T^{\ast} = s_h^{\ast} - 
abla\cdot\sigma_h^{\ast} with its mean equilibration and the remainder of the estimation are correct and unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed certified upper bound for \|\mathcal G(z_h)\|_{V^{\ast}} is incorrect. Any adjoint-enhanced output enclosure computed with this bound (including those in the numerical tables of Section 9) loses its guaranteed status. The abstract result thm:qoi:adjoint itself remains valid when supplied with the correct \|\mathcal G(z_h)\|_{V^{\ast}} bound.
issues.title: Sign error in adjoint residual flux-mismatch term
issues.why_classification: The wrong formula can produce an upper bound that is too small, invalidating the guarantee of the output enclosure. The repair is a contained sign correction in one formula and is a single local change that preserves the method, rate, and scope. It exceeds a pure typo because the formula encodes an incorrect identification of the physical flux (A\nabla z_h instead of -A\nabla z_h), and using it as written defeats the certified-enclosure guarantee, but no new proof architecture or lemma is required.
